title: Agent Harness configuration
description: The config seam. Everything project-specific the harness knows lives in harness.config.json at the repo root; the harness code requires nothing from the repo it grades. An absent or malformed config is a hard stop with a one-line fix, never a default: a harness that invents its own gate list prints a green verdict about a suite nobody agreed to. Every section may carry a `_readme` array of strings, because JSON has no comments and the explanation of a rule has to live next to the rule.

$schema.description: Path or URL to this schema, so an editor can validate and complete the file as you type it.

_readme.description: Prose about the file as a whole, as an array of lines. Carried through untouched; read by people, ignored by the harness.

project.description: What this repo is called, and where its prose lives.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

name.description: The repo's name in gate output and generated docs. Required: a report that does not say what it is about is a report that gets pasted into the wrong issue.

docsRoot.description: Root of the doc contract — frontmatter, line caps and the generated index all apply under here. Must stay inside the repo: a linter pointed outside the tree grades files no commit can fix.

tracksDir.description: Where a track folder lives (README.md, plan.md, traps.md, handoff.md, research/). Must stay inside the repo.

sourceBranch.description: OPTIONAL, and the one key here with no default. The branch every other branch's harness files are compared against by scripts/harness/branch-sync.js. Omit it and the script DETECTS the source: the remote's published head, then the first of main, master, trunk, default that exists as a ref, reported as a fallback so a guess is never read as a setting. State it only where detection would be wrong. One branch name, no whitespace. A branch that names itself here lands in source mode, where nothing is compared, so the script fails its manifest check when this disagrees with the remote's published head.

gates.description: THE GATE REGISTRY, in run order. Each entry is a command whose LAST stdout line is exactly `GATE <name> pass=<n> fail=<n> skipped=<n>`. pass+fail+skipped is the total, and the total is the load-bearing part: comparing only `pass` cannot tell a green run from a run where checks vanished. Must be non-empty — the harness has no default suite and will not guess one. Gates run in declaration order, because a build gate has to run before the check that grades what it produced.

_readme.description: Prose about the registry or this entry, as an array of lines.

name.description: Kebab-case identifier. It is the token in the GATE line, the key in gates.baseline.json, the argument to --only, and the stem of gates.red.<name>.log. `reproducible-build` is reserved for the artifact check.

command.description: A shell string, run from the repo root. A leading bare `node` is re-pointed at the runtime the harness is running under, so the suite is not graded by whichever node happens to be on PATH.

adapter.description: Only for a runner that prints its OWN summary and will not print a GATE line. Omit it and the GATE line is parsed. An unknown adapter is a hard error, never a fallback: a typo would otherwise read as a gate that crashed before its verdict and send the reader to the wrong file.

optional.description: true means an ABSENT TOOL declares a skip instead of a fail. It does not mean the gate is optional: a tool that is present and unhappy still fails. The skip is then red unless the caller passes --allow-skip <name>=1, so the decision to tolerate it stays in the invocation.

gateLine.description: The name the command actually prints in its GATE line, when it differs from `name`. This is how one script can be gated twice under two different environments.

artifacts.description: THE REPRODUCIBLE-BUILD CHECK. Every listed path is hashed before the suite and after it, and the gate `reproducible-build` is red unless each committed artifact is byte-identical to what this source produces — the defect being a source edit committed without a rebuild, which ships code no gate ever rendered while every other gate stays green. AN EMPTY LIST DECLARES ITSELF: the check prints `not applicable, 0 artifacts graded` and reports skipped=1 rather than passing silently, and that skip is red unless the caller passes --allow-skip reproducible-build=1.

oneOf.description: Just the files. Whichever declared gate rebuilds them is what this check grades.
The files plus the command that rebuilds them, for a repo whose build is not already a gate.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

command.description: The build command, run between the before and after hashes.

env.description: The secret-file stance, read by the PreToolUse env guard. The default is deny-all: a matched path is refused for reading, writing and shelling out to, whatever the tool asked.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

guarded.description: Patterns for the files no agent may open. Without them a credential file is one `cat` away from a transcript that leaves the machine.

openCarveOuts.description: The explicit exceptions to the deny-all stance. Every open carve-out is reported at SessionStart until it is removed, so the exception is something you keep seeing rather than something you forget.

path.description: The guarded file this carve-out opens.

why.description: Why it is open. An unexplained carve-out is never removed, because nobody can tell whether it is still needed.

until.description: YYYY-MM-DD expiry. Required: an undated carve-out is permanent by accident.

commitHygiene.description: Where working files are allowed to live, read by the commit-hygiene check. Without it the repo root accumulates scratch files — and the first casualty is the harness's own state, which lives beside its script precisely because a root-level baseline needed a waiver on every run, and a gate you waive routinely is a gate you have switched off.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

workDirs.description: The directories a working file belongs in. Anything else at the top level is a stray.

rootAllow.description: The files that legitimately sit at the repo root. Everything not listed is refused there.

docs.description: The doc contract's hard limits, read by the doc linter.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

caps.description: Line ceilings per document. `AGENTS.md` is the always-on policy file, so its ceiling is the tightest; `CLAUDE.md` is the stub that imports it, capped at the size of a pointer; `subtreeAgentsMd` is a per-directory AGENTS.md and the stub beside it; `default` applies to every other doc. Without a ceiling the file every session loads grows until it crowds out the work.

propertyNames.description: A document name, the key `subtreeAgentsMd`, or `default`.

additionalProperties.description: A positive integer number of lines. A cap of 0 is not `no cap`, it is a cap nothing can satisfy; a float compares strangely. Both are typos, neither is a policy, and both are rejected.

exemptDirs.description: Directories where frozen evidence lives. Research notes and archived tracks are dated and frozen on purpose, so a linter that rewrote them to fit a cap would be editing the record.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

budgetFile.description: A hand-written fixture of per-file ceilings that no script ever rewrites. A budget a tool can update records whatever happened rather than what was agreed, and the measurement then always agrees with itself.

tools.description: Which coding agents this repo is wired for. Absent means ["claude-code"]. Each id is a row of the tool registry, scripts/harness/tools.json, which records what that agent loads and what it can deny; `node scripts/harness/tools.js --check` fails on an id with no row. The loader checks only the shape, so the seam loads with no registry.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

enabled.description: Tool ids, each a registry row. An array in the file replaces the default whole. An unknown sub-key or a non-array is a hard stop, never a fallback: a list that quietly fell back to the default would report a tool as enabled that the file never named.

mode.description: The run mode the launcher (`harness run`) offers when it asks. A suggestion only: a person still accepts it at a terminal, and with no terminal the launcher refuses. It is never a mode in force, because this file is one the agent can edit.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

default.description: The mode offered on a bare Enter, or null to offer none. An unknown sub-key or an unknown mode is a hard stop, never a fallback.

worktrees.description: Where a workspace folder goes and what its branch is called (`harness worktree new`). A workspace is a linked git worktree: one folder per agent, each on its own branch over one shared history. Absent, both keys are derived, so a fresh clone needs no edit here.

_readme.description: Prose about this section, as an array of lines.

root.description: The folder new workspaces are created in, resolved against the main checkout, or null to derive it: the parent folder when the main checkout is a folder named `main` inside one, else a sibling `<repo>.worktrees`. It may not be inside any checkout; that is refused when a workspace is created.

branchPrefix.description: Prepended to a workspace name to make its branch name. Empty means the branch is the name.

artifactEntry.description: One committed artifact: a path string, { path } for a literal, or { glob } for a wildcard pattern. In a glob, `*` and `?` stay inside one path segment and `**/` crosses them.

oneOf.description: A repo-relative path, or a glob if it contains a wildcard.
A literal repo-relative path. An artifact listed here but absent on disk is a failing check, not a file that quietly drops out of the total.
A wildcard pattern expanded against the working tree at run time.
